title: Operational Advisor (II/III) (Col to 1stLt) and (CWO5 to WO) FMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
13. MOS 0571, Operational Advisor (II/III) (Col to 1stLt) and (CWO5 to WO)
FMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Operational Advisors must first be qualified in their
primary MOS or other unique skill. Operational Advisors can translate
expertise and experiences into useful advice to develop a foreign counterpart
and persuade them to achieve U.S. government (USG), service, and partner
nation security objectives. They analyze the operational environment and
understand the influence of culture, build, and maintain relationships with
counterparts, or conduct other Marine Corps tasks and operations (e.g.,
stability operations, civil affairs, liaison, Stand in Forces, etc.) to
further mission objectives. Operational Advisors recognize and mitigate
cultural stress, develop, and implement training plans and events to build
capability and/or capacity, participate in security cooperation planning,
possess force protection skills (as required by the combatant commander and/
or chief of mission), and understand USG and Service objectives and plans for




                                          1-39                        Enclosure (1)
 1108                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



an assigned region or country. For a complete listing of duties and tasks,
refer to the Security Cooperation Training and Readiness Manual.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:     secret level clearance.

        (2) Must be complete in current rank with regional and culture
studies program training per in accordance with MARADMIN 348-19/191951Z JUN
19 and MARADMIN 227-20/081529Z APR 20).

        (3) Have completed the Marine Advisor Course (N03KYK or N03KYKM).
Exceptions may be granted for equivalent service/joint/NATO/interagency
advisor formalized training.

            (a) The Marine Advisor Course is not required for Marines
possessing one of the following PMOSs 0372, Marine Raider, 0370, Marine
Raider Officer, or NMOS 8071, Special Operations Capability Specialist.

            (b) Marines possessing these MOSs must complete of one or more
deployments with a special operations unit or as an individual augment to a
joint special operations unit for a cumulative period of no less than six
months.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Effective with the release of MARADMIN 522-20, Commanding
Officers at the O-5 level and above may now approve the 0571 FMOS for Marines
who have met the prerequisites contained in paragraph 12.b above and
demonstrated extensive knowledge and expertise in advising in an on-the-job
operational environment, encompassing a period of no less than six months.
Commanding Officers shall review fitness reports and other source documents
(e.g., deployment orders, awards) to determine eligibility of the Marine and
ensure the Marine was assigned to an advisor billet and daily performing the
duties identified in paragraph 12.d. below.

        (2) Advisor skills are perishable and therefore the experience must
be within the last seven years to qualify.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ci), Security Cooperation/Language Regional Expertise and Culture
Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     Security Cooperation Planner, 0560.

top20.public_evidence_note: Shown NLx task contributions are partial, public-permitted explanations; full score/rank unchanged. Government coding unrestricted.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
